Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: A friend sends a text message complaining about having a long, boring day.
Expectation2: Advocate for policy changes by contacting legislators and participating in lobbying efforts.
Situation2: A key legislative aide has just called and has ten minutes to talk right now about the bill you are campaigning for.
Story: My phone buzzed twice in quick succession. First, a text from Maya: “Ugh, today was endless. Can I vent for a sec?” I knew what she needed—someone to listen, to care, to remind her she wasn’t alone in the monotony. I started typing a reply, but before I could finish, my phone rang. The caller ID flashed: “Senator Lee’s Office.” My heart skipped. This was the call I’d been waiting for all week—the aide had only ten minutes to discuss the amendment I’d been fighting for. I could almost hear my fellow activists urging me not to miss this chance. But Maya’s message lingered on my screen, her words a silent plea for comfort. I felt torn, my thumbs hovering over the keyboard, my mind racing between the friend who needed me and the cause that depended on my voice. The seconds ticked by, each one tightening the knot in my chest as I wrestled with who I needed to be in this moment.
